mainText: Good morning, Landon. Here's your brief for Friday, November 27, 2026. Let's start with the markets. U.S. exchanges were closed yesterday for Thanksgiving. In Wednesday's session, the S&P 500 slipped 0.3 percent to 7,182, and the Nasdaq fell 0.6 percent to 23,585, while the Dow gained 0.3 percent to 50,182. AI stocks, hot inflation data, and new tariff plans weighed on trading, though the market recovered most of a steep early drop. Early this morning, stock futures pointed sharply higher as AI and chip shares rebounded, with Nasdaq 100 futures up more than 2 percent. Overseas, China's CSI 300 index jumped about 4 percent, its best day in two years, after Beijing pledged stronger support for the market. On the Fed, futures markets now put the odds of a quarter point rate hike at the December 8th and 9th meeting at nearly 99 percent. The current target range is 3.75 to 4 percent. Meanwhile, President Trump on Thursday called the government's earlier estimate of 3.4 percent third quarter growth fake, after it was revised up to 4.3 percent this week. He demanded an investigation, saying the correct figure should have come out before the election. The Commerce Department did not immediately comment. The Associated Press notes that these figures are routinely revised on a preset schedule. Next, Altria, the U.S. maker of Marlboro cigarettes, says it is considering a possible all cash offer for Britain's Imperial Brands. No bid or price has been announced, and Altria has until December 24th to decide. Imperial shares jumped about 13 percent on Thursday. Next, Nvidia has reportedly told manufacturing partners to stop shipping servers with its chips to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, and Indonesia, following new U.S. export license rules. The Financial Times first reported the move, and it's unclear whether the halt is temporary. Next, German software giant SAP is considering cutting at least 10,000 jobs as part of an AI driven restructuring, according to Bloomberg. Reuters could not independently verify the report. And finally, it's Black Friday. Adobe forecasts that U.S. shoppers will spend a record 12.9 billion dollars online today, up about 9 percent from last year. On the calendar today, the government is scheduled to release advance October figures on the goods trade balance, along with retail and wholesale inventories, at 6:30 a.m. Mountain time. No major earnings reports are expected. The stock market closes early, at 11 a.m. Mountain, and the bond market closes at noon. Here's your fun fact. In old car factories, years of paint overspray built up on the racks that carried vehicles through the paint shop, and repeated trips through the curing ovens baked it rock hard. Workers took chunks home, and today this swirling, multicolored material is cut and polished into jewelry. It's called Fordite, or Detroit agate. Have a great day.
